cohort: 78 infants with brachial plexus injuries recognized at or after delivery between October 2003 and March 2013 at a single academic medical institution
finding: Brachial plexus injuries occurred as frequently in multiparous patients as in nulliparous patients, despite multiparous patients having shorter labor courses, fewer labor interventions, and larger infants, though providers significantly underestimated the birth weight of infants born to multiparous mothers.
mod_finding: Of the 78 brachial plexus injuries, 71 (91%) occurred after a vaginal delivery and 7 (9%) after a cesarean delivery.
birth_weight: Median birth weight was 4060 g in the multiparous group and 3591 g in the nulliparous group
